name: The Brethren of the Theragatha
credit: Jataka relief (the jackal and the otters) from the Bharhut stupa, 2nd century BCE, a seated ascetic among animals; an early Buddhist relief, not a likeness of any thera · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: The Thera-gāthā, the “Verses of the Elder Monks”, is the Pali canon’s collection of poems by early Buddhist monks, in the Khuddaka Nikāya, the companion of the Therī-gāthā of the nuns. Each psalm is traditionally ascribed to a named thera, from chief disciples such as Sāriputta, Moggallāna and Ānanda to a fisherman, a barber, a potter and a former brigand, and a few are given to groups of friends. The attributions are traditional, and the date and authorship of the verses remain uncertain.

The translation is Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids’s Psalms of the Brethren, the second volume of Psalms of the Early Buddhists, published in 1913 for the Pali Text Society. It numbers 264 psalms in twenty-one cantos, arranged by length from single verses to the seventy-one verses of Vangisa. The archive gives the verses only; the commentary’s origin-stories, Rhys Davids’s notes and her introductions are omitted.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren I: Subhuti
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Well-roofed and pleasant is my little hut,
And screened from winds — Rain at thy will, thou god!
My heart is well composed, my heart is free,
And ardent is my mood. Now rain, god! rain.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren II: Kotthita the Great
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Whoso, serene and calm, dead to the world,
Can utter wisdom’s runes, with wit unswelled,
Unruffled — he doth shake off naughty things
As they were forest leaves by wind-god blown.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren III: Kankha-Revata
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Behold how great the wisdom is of Them
Who Thus-have-come! As fire at midnight hour,
Givers of light, givers of sight are they
To those that pass, subduing all their doubt.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren IV: Punna of the Mantanis
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Aye with the good consort, with them
Who know, who understand, who see the Good.
Great is the Good and deep and hard to see,
Subtle and delicately fine, to which
The wise and brave do penetrate, e’en they
Who strenuous live and lofty vision gain.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren V: Dabba
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Once hard to tame, by taming tamed is now
Dabba, from doubts released, content, serene.
Victor is Dabba now, and void of fears;
Perfected he and staunch in steadfastness.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren VI: SIta-Vaniya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
There is a brother who to Cool Wood gone doth dwell
Alone, content, in meditative ecstasy,
Victorious, no more by creeping dread dismayed,
He mindful watcheth over sense with courage high.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren VII: Bhalliya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Whoso hath chased away the Death-king and his host,
E’en as a mighty flood the causeway of frail reeds,
Victor is he, self-tamed. Fear cometh never more.
His is the Goal supreme, and utter steadfastness.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren VIII: Vira
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren IX: Pilinda-Vaccha
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
O welcome this that came, nor came amiss!
O goodly was the counsel given to me!
’Mong divers doctrines mooted among men
Of all ’twas sure the Best I sought and found.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren X: Punnamasa
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
All longings as to this or other life
Have I put far from me, as one who hath
Beta’en himself to truth, whose heart’s at peace,
Who, self -subdued, in all things undefiled,
Discerns the world’s incessant ebb and flow.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XI: Gavaccha the Less
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Abundantly this brother doth rejoice,
For the blest truths the Buddha hath revealed
Are his, and he hath won the Path of Peace,
And his the bliss where worldly cares are stilled.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XII: Gavaccha the Great
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
In wisdom strong, guided by virtue’s rule, intent,
To concentration’s rapture given, yet vigilant;
Partaking of such fare as brings thee only good:
So in the faith, with passions quenched, await the hour.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XIII: Vanavaccha
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Crags with the hue of heaven’s blue clouds,
Where lies enbosomed many a shining tarn
Of crystal-clear, cool waters, and whose slopes
The ‘herds of Indra’ cover and bedeck:
Those are the braes wherein my soul delights.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XIV: Sivaka
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
The teacher spake me thus: Sivaka, hence
Let’s go I’ Here in the town my body dwells;
My thoughts are to the forest gone. So thus,
Prostrated though I be, yet do I go.
No bond is there for those who understand.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XV: Kunda-Dhana
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Five cut thou off; Five leave behind, and Five beyond all cultivate!
He who the Fivefold Bond transcends — a Brother
Flood-crossed is he called.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XVI: Belatthasisa
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
E’en as the high-bred steer with crested back
Lightly the plough adown the furrow turns,
So lightly glide for me the nights and days
Now that this pure untainted bliss is won.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XVII: Dasaka
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Who waxes slothful and in diet gross,
Given to sleep and rolling as he lies,
Like a great hog with provender replete—
The dolt comes hack again, again to birth.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XVIII: Singala-Pitar
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Lo! in the forest of Bhesakala
A brother dwells, heir of the Buddha’s grace,
Suffusing through and through this earthy frame
With thought intent, austere, of skeleton.
Beshrew me, if he do not swiftly drive
All passion of the senses clean away!

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XIX: Kula
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
The conduit-makers lead the stream,
Fletchers coerce the arrow-shaft,
The joiners mould the wooden plank;
The self — ’tis that the pious tame.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XX: Ajita
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
All unafraid of death, nor fain to live,
I shall lay down this compound frame anon,
With mind alert, with consciousness controlled.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XXI: Nigrodha
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
No fear have I of fearsome things, for He,
Our Master, knoweth well th’ ambrosial lore.
The Path where fear nowise a footing finds,
Along that Path the brethren hold their way.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XXII: Cittaka
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Peacocks of sapphire neck and comely crest
Calling, calling in Karaijviya woods
By cool and humid winds made musical:
They wake the thinker from his noonday sleep.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XXIII: Gosala
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Lo! I who in the bamboo thicket dined
Off rice and honey, who now comprehend,
Him worshipping, the ebb and flux of all
These factors of my life, will hie me back
Up on my hill, to foster there the growth
Of heart’s detachment, lone and separate.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XXIV: Sugandha
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Scarce have the rains gone by since I went forth,
Yet see the seemly order of the Norm!
The Threefold Wisdom have I gotten now
And done all that the Buddha bids us do.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XXV: Nandiya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
‘O Evil One! what canst thou do with those that have
transcended thy realm? ’Tis thou that thereby wilt meet with defeat and ruin
To him whose thought is ever newly born
From splendour of the Path, and eke hath touched
The Fruit — if such a Brother thou assail st,
Black-hearted sprite, to misery thou must go.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XXVI: Abhaya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Of him, the Buddha, kin o’ th’ sun, I heard
The word most eloquent, and hearing pierced
The subtle truth of things, as ’twere the tip
Of hair by cunning bowman’s art transfixed.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XXVII: Lomasakangiya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Dabba and Kusa grass and pricking stems
And all that hurts in brush and underwood
Forth from my breast I’ll push and thrust away,
And go where I the growth may cultivate
Of heart’s detachment, lone and separate.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XXVIII: Jambugamika’s Son
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
And art thou then not gratified by gear?
And art thou then not charmed thyself t’ adorn?
And is this fragrant odour, virtue-fraught,
Wafted by thee, and not by other folk?

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XXIX: Harita
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Now bend aloft thyself; e’en as his holt
The fletcher, so do thou, O Harita,
Make straight thy heart and ignorance cut away.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XXX: Uttiya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Since sickness hath befallen me, O now
Let there arise in me true mindfulness.
Sickness hath now befallen me — ’tis time
For me no more to dally or delay.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XXXI: Gahvaratiriya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
In the great forest, in the mighty woods,
Touched though I be by gadfly and by gnat,
I yet would roam, like warrior-elephant,
In van of battle, mindful, vigilant.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XXXII: Suppiya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
O would that I who hourly waste, might change
For that which ne’er decays — who ever burn,
Might change for that cool bliss— e’en for the Peace
That passeth all, Safety beyond compare!

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XXXIII: Sopaka
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
E’en as she would be very good
Towards her only child, her well-beloved son,
So too ye should be very good
Towards all creatures everywhere and everyone.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XXXIV: Posiya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Best when not near, both now and evermore,
Are such as these for him who understands.
Forth from the township to the woods I went,
Thence to my home once more I came; but thence
Rising I gat me forth again, nor e’er
Did this same Posiya let fall a word.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XXXV: Samannakani
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Happiness he who seeks may win an he practise the seeking —
Honour he gaineth beside, and growth of renown shall befall him —
So he but practise the road called Straight, even the Ariyan,
The Noble Eightfold Path whereby we may reach salvation.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XXXVI: Kuma’s Son
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
O goodly are the things our ears now hear!
O goodly is the life we here may lead!
O good it is always to lack a house!
Now questioning on things of high import,
Now showing all due thanks and reverence:
Such is the calling of the true recluse,
Of him who owneth naught of anything.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XXXVII: The Comrade of Kuma’s Son
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
To divers regions back and forth they fare
Heedless of heart upon their rounds, and balk
The mind’s due concentration. What, forsooth,
Shall all this vagabondage bring to pass?
Hence is it meet that clamour be subdued,
Nor harass him who fain would meditate.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XXXVIII: Gavampati
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Who by his might reared up the Sarabhu,
Who standeth self-reliant and unmoved,
Who hath transcended every tie, Gavampati,
Him mighty seer the very gods acclaim,
Surpasser of the coming back to be.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XXXIX: Tissa
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
As one downsmitten by impending sword,
As one whose hair and turban are aflame,
So let the Brother, mindful and alert,
Go forth, all worldly passions left behind.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XL: Vaddhamana
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
As one downsmitten by impending sword,
As one whose hair and turban are aflame,
So let the Brother, mindful and alert,
Go forth, all lust of living left behind.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XLI: Sirivaddha
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
The lightnings flash e’en in the rocky cave,
Smiting Vebhara’s crest and Pandava,
And, in the mountain-bosom hid, a child
Of that incomparable Master sits
Ardent in contemplative ecstasy.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XLII: Khadira-Vaniya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Come, Cala, and you, Upacala too,
Sisupacala also, take good heed,
Be on your guard, for he who comes to you
Is as a wondrous archer splitting hairs.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XLIII: Sumangala
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Well rid, well rid, O excellently rid
Am I from these three crooked tasks and tools,
Rid o’ my reaping with your sickles, rid
Of trudging after ploughs, and rids my back
Of bending o’er these wretched little spades.
Though they he ever here, ay, ever here,
Enough of them, I say, for me, enough!
Go meditate, Sumangala, ay, go
And meditate, Sumangala, and bide
Earnest and diligent, Sumangala!

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XLIV: Sanu
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Mother, they weep for the dead, or the living they may not see.
But for him, O mother, who lives, who is here, why mournest thou me?

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XLV: Ramaniyaviharin
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
E’en though he trip and fall, the mettled brute
Of noble breed will steadfast stand once more.
So look on me as one who having learned
Of Him, the All-Enlightened One, have gained
True insight, am become of noble breed,
And of the Very Buddha very child.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XLVI: Samiddhi
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
In ti list and hope forth from my home I came
Into the homeless life. And there in me
Have mindfulness and insight grown, and tense
And well composed my heart and mind. Make thou
Whatever shams thou list, thou’lt harm me not.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XLVII: Ujjaya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Buddha the Wake, the Hero hail! all hail!
Thou who from every bond art wholly free!
Strong in the lore I learnt of thee, I live
From fourfold venom cleansed, sane, immune.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XLVIII: Sanjaya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Since I went forth from home to homeless life,
Ne’er have I harboured conscious wish or plan
Un-Ariyan, or linked with enmity.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XLIX: Ramaneyyaka
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Not all the clitter-clatter of your noise,
No more than chirp and squeal of forest sounds,
Avail to make pulse throb or mind distraught,
For one the aim to which my heart is given.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren L: Vimala
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
The burdened earth is sprinkled by the rain,
The winds blow cool, the lightnings roam on high.
Eased and allayed th’ obsessions of the mind,
And in my heart the spirit’s mastery.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LI: Godhika
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
God rains as ’twere a melody most sweet.
Snug is my little hut, sheltered, well-roofed.
The heart of me is steadfast and at peace.
Now an it pleaseth thee to rain, god, rain!

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LII: Subahu
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
God rains as ’twere a melody most sweet.
Snug is my little hut, sheltered, well-roofed,
Well hath my mind the body’s nature grasped.
Now an it pleaseth thee to rain, god, rain!

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LIII: Valliya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
God rains as ’twere a melody most sweet.
Snug is my little hut, sheltered, well-roofed.
Herein earnest and strenuous I dwell.
Now an it pleaseth thee to rain, god, rain!

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LIV: Uttiya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
God rains as ’twere a melody most sweet.
Snug is my little hut, sheltered, well-roofed.
Herein I dwell unmated and alone.
Now an it pleaseth thee to rain, god, rain!

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LV: Anjana-vaniya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Deep in the leafy glades of An j ana
My couch into a little hut I made.
The threefold wisdom have I made my own,
And all the Buddha’s ordinance is done.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LVI: Kutiviharin
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Who’s in my little hut? A brother ’tis,
Who in thy little hut, all passions tamed,
Hath throughly set his mind. Know this, O friend,
’Twas not for naught thou mad’st thy little hut!

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LVII: Kutiviharin (2)
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
This was an ancient hut, say’st thou? To build
Another hut, a new one, is thy wish?
O cast away the longing for a hut!
New hut will bring new pain, brother, to thee.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LVIII: Ramaniyakutika
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Delightful is my little hut, the gift
Most fair of faithful, pious folk.
What need of maidens then have I? Nay, go
Thither to them, ye women, who have need of you.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LIX: Kosalaviharin
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Strong in my faith I left the world. Now here
Within the woods a hut is made for me;
And I with zeal and ardour meditate,
With watchful wit and clarity of mind.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LX: Sivali
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Now have they prospered, all my highest aims,
To compass which I sought this still retreat.
The holy lore and liberty, my quest,
All lurking vain conceits I cast away.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXI: Vappa
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
He who doth see can see another seer,
Him too who hath no eyes wherewith to see,
He who himself sees not, can ne’er discern
Either the eye that sees not, or the seer.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXII: Vajji-putta
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Each by himself we in the forest dwell,
Like logs rejected by the woodman’s craft.
And many a one doth envy me my lot,
E’en as the hell-bound him who fares to heaven.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXIII: Pakkha
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
They fly at what is fall’ll, and as it lies,
Swooping in greed they come again, again. . . .
But what ’twas meet to do, that have I done,
And what is verily delectable,
Therein was my delight: thus happily
Has happiness been sought after and won.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXIV: Vimala-Kondanna
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
By the bright Banner came I here to birth
In her called of the Tree. And by the flag
That smites the flag, is the great Flag o’er-thrown.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXV: Ukkhepakata-Vaccha
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
That heaped wealth by Yaccha’s toil thrown up
By steady increment these many years,
That doth he to the laity declare,
Seated in honour, filled with splendid joy.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXVI: Meghiya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
He, the great Hero, counselled me, whose mind
Hath all transcended that our minds may know.
And I, hearing the Norm, held close to Him
In loving pupillage and piety.
The threefold wisdom have I made my own,
And all the Buddha’s ordinance is done.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXVII: Ekadhamma Savaniya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Burnt up in me is all that doth defile,
And rooted out all life’s continuance;
Slain utterly the cycle of re-birth:
Now is there no more coming back to be.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXVIII: Ekudaniya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
He who doth dwell on highest plane of thought,
With zeal unfaltering, Sage, Arahant,
In wisdom’s branches trained such as he is,
No sorrows may beset him, who with mind
Calm and serene and clear abideth aye.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXIX: Channa
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
I heard the Truth which that Great One had taught,
And felt its mighty virtues, known by Him
Who all things with supernal insight knew.
The Path for winning things ambrosial
I found. Past-master He in sooth to guide
Into the way of blest security.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXX: Punna
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Only virtue here is highest; but the wise man is supreme.
He who wisdom hath and virtue,
He ’mong men and gods is victor.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXXI: Vacchapala
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Is there a man who can the truth discern
Tho’ it be very subtle and refined,
Who, skilled to measure spiritual growth,
Is yet of lowly and of gentle mind,
Who shapes his life by rule of Them that Wake:
For him Nibbana is not hard to find.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXXII: Atuma
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
As the new bamboo-stem, even when grown
To its full knotted height, can scarce emerge,
So I by all this bringing home of brides —
Give me your leave! Gone forth e’en now am I.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXXIII: Manava
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
I saw an aged one, and one afflicted with disease,
And then I saw one dead, with all his span of life consumed.
Thence I forth going left the world to live the other life,
And from me put away the enticing sweets of sense-desire.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXXIV: Suyamana
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
With sensuous desires, with enmity,
With sloth of mind and torpor of the flesh
A brother hath no truck, and in his heart
Turmoil of any kind and doubt are dead.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXXV: Susarada
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
O goodly is the sight of cultured minds!
Doubt is cut off, and wisdom grows apace.
E’en of a fool they make an able man;
Hence goodly is the intercourse with saints.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXXVI: Piyanjaha
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Where men are arrogant, see thou lie low.
Where they are low in mind, lift up the heart.
Dwell thou where other folk care not to dwell,
Wherein men find delight, take thou no joy.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXXVII: Hattharoha-Putta
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Once roamed this heart a-field, a wanderer
Wherever will, or whim, or pleasure led.
To-day that heart I’ll hold in thorough check,
As trainer’s hook the savage elephant.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXXVIII: Mendasira
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Full many a round of rebirth have I run
Nor found a clue. Lo! now from me who sore
Have suffered is the load of ill withdrawn.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXXIX: Rakkhita
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXXX: Ugga
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
All action wrought by me and bringing birth,
Whether ’twas of great potency or small,
Shattered and ended is it utterly.
Now is there no more coming back to be.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXXXI: Samitigutta
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Whatso of evil wrought in bygone days,
In former births by me, just here and now,
Tis that whereby I lie and suffer sore —
But other ground for ill exists no more!

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXXXII: Kassapa
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
To any place where alms are easy got,
Where’er ’tis safe and free from peril, there
Go thou, my boy; vex not thy life with care.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXXXIII: Siha
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
O Siha! persevere in earnestness;
By night and day abide unfaltering.
Engender the good Norm within thy heart.
Swiftly renounce that piled up base of birth.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXXXIV: Nita
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Thou all the night to slumber given o’er,
Who lov’st the day ’mid chattering crowds to spend: —
Dost deem that thou this way at any time,
Poor silly fool, of Ill shalt make an end?

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXXXV: Sunaga
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Expert to grasp the image conjured up,
Versed in the secret of the life detached,
Practised in contemplation, clear in mind: —
Well may he win to rapture unalloyed.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXXXVI: Nagita
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Outside our Order many others be, who teach
A path never, like this one, to Nibbana leading.
But us the Exalted One, the blessed Master’s self
Instructs as ’twere by just the palm o’ th’ hand outspreading.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXXXVII: Pavittha
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
The factors of the self are throughly seen;
All bases of new being broken down.
Slain utterly the cycle of rebirth.
Now is there no more coming back to be.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXXXVIII: Ajjuna
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
O wonder that I found the power to draw
Myself forth from the waters on dry land.
Borne drifting on the awful flood I learnt
To know the Truths, their truth to understand.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren LXXXIX: Devasabha
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Transcended is the miry bog of lusts.
Past doom infernal am I safely come
From flood and fetter dire to liberty,
And shed is every form of self conceit.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XC: Samidatta
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
The factors of my life well understood
Stand yet a little while with severed root.
Slain is the round of living aye renewed.
Now is there no more coming back to be.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XCI: Paripunnaka
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Never as ’t were some dish of hundred essences,
Could I o’errate what I partook to-day,
When He, the all-seeing Gotama, the Buddha blest,
Himself revealed to me the holy Norm.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XCII: Vijaya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XCIII: Eraka
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Woeful are worldly wishes, Eraka!
No weal in worldly wishes, Eraka!
Whoso desireth joys of sense desireth ill.
Whoso desires not joys of sense desires no ill.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XCIV: Mettaji
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
All glory to the Exalted One,
Our splendid Lord, the Sakiyas’ son!
For he the topmost height hath won,
And well the Norm supreme hath shown.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XCV: Cakkhupala
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
All blind am I and perished are mine eyes
And through the jungle’s wilderness I fare.
E’en then I’ll go, and were it lying down,
But not with child of evil as my mate.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XCVI: Khandasumana
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
One flower in pious offering brought
Did win me years on years of pleasant life
In heavenly worlds; the balance hath availed
To bring me perfect peace and purity.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XCVII: Tissa
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Renouncing costly vessels wrought in bronze,
In gold and lac, I grasped this earthen bowl.
The second time was I anointed then.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XCVIII: Abhaya (2)
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Sight of fair shape bewildering self-control,
If one but heed the image sweet and dear,
The heart inflamed in feeling doth o’erflow
And clinging stayeth. Thus in him do grow
The deadly taints that bring new living near.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren XCIX: Uttiya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Sound of sweet voice bewildering self-control,
If one but think upon the image dear,
The heart inflamed in feeling doth o’erflow
And clinging stayeth. Thus in him do grow
The deadly taints that bring Sapsara near.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren C: Devasabha (2)
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Whoso supreme endeavour doth put forth,
Whose range is in the fourfold heedfulness,
He with fair flowers of Liberty enwreathed,
Sane and immune, will reach the perfect peace.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CI: Belatthakani
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Though layman’s life be left, yet if the task
Remain undone, the mouth harsh furrows plough,
The paunch be full, the mind all slack with sloth: —
Like a great hog with provender replete,
He cometh back, again, again to birth.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CII: Setuccha
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
By vain conceits deluded, and their minds
Corrupted by the varied things of sense;
Flushed by their gains, by dearth thereof upset,
They fail to win the concentrated mind.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CIII: Bandhura
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Nay, ’tis not this I need, who live in bliss,
Regaled by sweetest nectar of the Norm.
Drinking those drops peerless, supreme, shall I
Forsooth my tongue with poison now acquaint?

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CIV: Khitaka
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Buoyant in sooth my body, every pulse
Throbbing in wondrous bliss and ecstasy.
Even as cotton-down blown on the breeze,
So floats and hovers this my body light.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CV: Malitavambha
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Where I am straitened let me never dwell,
Let me go thence, if life too pleasant prove.
Ne’er will the man with eyes to see abide
Where aught may hinder in the quest supreme.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CVI: Suhemanta
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
A hundred tokens show, a hundred marks
Betray wherein the hidden meaning lies.
Whoso hath eyes to see but one, a dullard is,
Who can discern the hundred, he is wise.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CVII: Dhammasava
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
I pondered well, then sought the life that lay
Beyond the walls and bonds of household life.
The Threefold Wisdom have I made my own,
And all the Buddha’s ordinance is done.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CVIII: Dhammasava’s Father
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
A hundred years was I and eke a score,
When forth I went and knew my home no more.
The Threefold Wisdom have I made my own,
And all the Buddha’s ordinance is done.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CIX:
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Not yet doth he, though in retreat he dwell,
Con o’er the system by that Blest One (planned)
Who showed compassion for our highest good.
Still are his powers relaxed and uncontrolled,
Like woodland doe all tender grown and weak.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CX: Usabha
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
The trees on high by towering cloud refreshed
With the new rain break forth in verdant growth.
To Usabha who for detachment longs,
And hath the forest sense of things, doth come
[From this responsive spring] abundant good.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXI: Jenta
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Hard is the life without the world, and hard
In sooth to bear house life. Deep is the Norm;
Hard too is wealth to win. Thus difficult
The choice of one or other how to live.
Behoves me bear unceasingly in mind
[And see in everything] Impermanence.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXII: Vacchagotta
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
The Threefold Lore is mine, and I excel
In Jhana-ecstasy, adept in calm
Of balanced mind. Salvation have I won,
And all the Bnddha-ordinance is done.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXIII: Vanavaccha (2)
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Crags where clear waters lie, a rocky world,
Haunted by black-faced apes and timid deer,
Where ’neath bright blossoms run the silver streams:
Those are the highlands of my heart’s delight.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXIV: Adhimutta
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
If ye to this gross body give such heed,
Greedy its pleasures to enjoy, the while
Life’s energies do ebb away, O whence
Shall come perfection in the holy life?

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXV: Mahanama
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Lo thou! how to a wretched end art come
By this steep crag, this famous Hunter s Hill,
Its many crests begirt by sal-tree woods,
[And all its glens with tangled verdure] clothed!

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXVI: Parapariya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Avoiding truck with contact’s sixfold field,
Guarding the gates of sense, master of self,
The general root of misery vomiting,
From every poison-taint am I immune.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXVII: Yasa
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
With perfumed skin and delicately clad
And head ablaze with gems, natheless my way
I found and made the Threefold Lore my own;
And now the Buddha-ordinance is done.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXVIII: Kimbila
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
As bidden by some power age o’er her falls.
Her shape is as another, yet the same.
Now this my self, who ne’er have left myself,
Seems other than the self I recollect.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXIX: Vajji-putta (2)
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Come thou and plunge in leafy lair of trees,
Suffer Nibbana in thy heart to sink!
Study and dally not, thou Gotamid!
What doth this fingle-f angle mean to thee?

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXX: Isidatta
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
The factors of my life well understood
Stand yet a little while with severed root.
Sorrow is slain! that quest I’ve won, and won
Is purity from fourfold Venom’s stain.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXXI: Uttara
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
There is no life that lasteth evermore,
Nor permanence in things from causes come.
They are reborn, the factors of our life,
Thereafter they dissolve and die away.

Since this the evil claiming all my thought,
Sooth am I one who doth not seek to be.
Detached from all that worldly aims commend,
Of th’ intoxicants have I now made an end.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXXII: Pindola-Bharadvaja
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Not without rule and method must we live.
But food as such is never near my heart.
‘By nutriment the body is sustained’:
This do I know, and hence my quest for alms.

These bows and gifts and treats from wealthy folk.
’Tis like steel splinter bedded in the flesh,
For foolish brethren hard to extricate.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXXIII: Valliya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Within the little five-doored hut an ape
Doth prowl, and round and round from door to door
He hies, rattling with blows again, again.

Halt, ape! run thou not forth! for thee
Tis not herein as it was wont to be.
Reason doth hold thee captive. Never more
Shalt roam far hence [in freedom as of yore].

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXXIV: Gangatiriya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
On Ganga’s shore three palm-tree leaves I took
And made my hut; my bowl like funeral pot
Wherewith men sprinkle milk upon a corpse;
My cloak from refuse of the dust-heap culled.

Two years, from one rain-season till the next,
I [there abode], nor spake a word save once.
So till the third year passed— then the long night
Of gloom asunder burst [and broke in light].

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXXV: Ajina
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
E’en though a man have gained the Triple Lore,
Have vanquished death and purged th intoxicants,
Yet, let him be to fame unknown, poor fools
May in their ignorance look down on him.

But let him get the good things of this world,
Then though he be of evil breed, natheless
Service and honour will they render him.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXXVI: Melajina
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
When I had heard the Master preach the Norm,
No doubts my mind could thenceforth entertain
In him all-knowing and invincible.

Nor in a mighty hero like to him,
Lord of the caravan, driver of men,
Peerless and grand, nor in the Path, the Rule,
Can ever want of faith disturb my soul.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXXVII: Radha
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
E’en as into an ill-roofed house the rain
Doth pierce and penetrate continually,
So into mind by exercise untrained
Doth passion ever pierce and penetrate.

And as into a well-roofed house no rain
Doth pierce and penetrate continually,
So into mind by calm and insight trained
Doth passion never pierce and penetrate.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXXVIII: Suradha
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
All coming back to birth is now destroyed.
The Conqueror’s Rule hath guided all my ways.
That which we call the Net have I put off;
The lust that leads to life is rooted out.

And the great quest, for which I left the world,
Forsaking home a homeless life to lead,
Even that quest and high reward I’ve won,
For I am he whose bonds are riven in twain.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXXIX: Gotama
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
At ease they sleep, the wise and pure, who ne’er
Are bound to womankind, for these must aye
Be kept ’neath watch and ward, and among them
’Tis ever hard to learn the truth of things.

War to the knife with thee, O lust, we’ve waged.
Now are we quit and free of debt to thee.
Now fare we onward to that Going-out,
Where at our journey’s end we weep no more.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXXX: Vasabha
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
He erst doth work destruction to himself;
Thereafter doth he ruin other men.
Most throughly works he mischief to himself,
E’en as decoy-bird by its own deceit.

No brahmin he, by outward colour judged.
By inner hue shall ye the brahmin know.
He in whom deeds show evil, even he
Is swarth of face, O consort of Suja.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXXXI: Cunda the Great
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
The will to learn maketh of learning growth;
Learning makes insight grow, and by insight
We know the Good; known Good brings bliss along.

Seek ye the lonely haunts remote from men.
Practise the life of liberty from Bonds.
If there ye come not by your heart’s desire,
Dwell with the Brethren, mindful and controlled.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXXXII: Jotidasa
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
They who in divers ways by deeds of force
And violence, rude and rough-mannered folk,
Do work their fellow-creatures injury,
Thereby they too themselves are overthrown,
For never is th’ effect of action lost.

The deed a man doth, be it good or ill,
To all his doing is he verily the heir.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXXXIII: Herannakani
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
The days, the nights flit by and pass away.
Life is arrested, and the span
To mortals given is consumed and fails,
Like water in the shallow mountain streams.

But evil actions still the fool commits,
Nor understands how dire the aftermath,
Till comes the bitter hour of action’s fruit.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXXXIV: Somamitta
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
As one who, mounted on a puny plank,
Is in mid-ocean whelm’d beneath the waves,
So even he of blameless life doth sink,
When thrown together with the man of sloth;
Wherefore from such an one keep well apart
The sluggard and the poor in energy

Dwell thou with them who live aloof,
With wise, with noble souls who have renounced,
Who in rapt contemplation ever strive.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXXXV: Sabbamitta
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Folk are bound up with folk and cling to folk.
Folk suffer scathe from folk and wreak the same.

What boots thee then this folk, and brood of folk?
Let the folk go and get thee gone from them,
Who as they go injure so many folk.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXXXVI: Mahakala
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Kali, woman broad and swart of hue as blackbird,
Now hath broken off a thighbone, now another;
Now hath broken off an arm, and now another;
Now the skull hath broken off as ’twere a milk bowl,
Made them ready and is seated.

He who witless doth not understand, but maketh
Cause for life renewed, comes back again to sorrow.
Wherefore he who knows creates no more new causes.
May I ne’er so lie again with scattered members!

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXXXVII: Tissa
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Many the foes he gets, the bhikkhu shorn,
Wrapt in his robe, to whom the world gives gifts
Of food and drink, raiment and where to lodge.

Let him then, knowing all the bane herefrom,
The fearsome peril in the world’s regard,
Taking but little, free from lusting’s taint,
Wary and mindful, hold his onward way.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXXXVIII: Kimbila
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Where lies the Eastern Bamboo Grove we dwell,
Sons of the Sakiyans, comrades [all and true].
No little wealth have we renounced for this,
Contented with whatever fills our bowl.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXXXIX: Nanda
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Heedless and shallow once my thoughts were set
On all the bravery of outward show;
Fickle was I and frivolous; all my days
Were worn with wanton sensuality.

But by the Buddha’s skilful art benign,
Who of sun’s lineage cometh, was I brought
To live by deeper thought, whereby my heart
From the great swamp of endless life I drew.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXL: Sirimat
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Others may laud and honour him
Whose self is uncontrolled.
Surely amiss their praise is given,
Since self is uncontrolled.

Others may chide and censure him
Whose self is well controlled.
Surely amiss their blame is given,
Since self is well controlled.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXLI: Uttara
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Well do I understand the factors five,
And well is craving rooted out in me,
Developed are the seven wisdom-chords,
And all the poison-fumes are shrunk to nought.

And since the factors now are understood,
I— look you! — casting out the Huntress fell
[Who sets her netted snare for every thought],
And cultivating wisdom’s harmony,
Sane and immune, in peace shall pass away.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXLII: Bhaddaji
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Panada was that king by name
Whose palace was of gold;
Sixteen apartments deep it stood,
Aloft a thousandfold.

A thousand flights it rose on high,
Its walls with scroll-work dight,
With many a flaunting banner hung,
With emeralds glittering bright.
’Twas there they danced, Gandharvas danced,
Six thousand in seven bands.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXLIII: Sobhita
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
A bhikkhu mindful, gifted with insight,
With strenuous effort strongly set to work,
Have I [the infinite past] recalled to mind:
Five hundred ages in a single night.

O let the Onsets Four of mindfulness
My study be, the Seven, the noble Eight!
For I [the infinite past] have called to mind:
Five hundred ages in a single night.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXLIV: Valliya
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
All that by earnest work has to be done,
All that one fain to wake to truth must do,
All that shall be my work nor shall I fail.
O see my forward strides in energy!

And do thou show me how and where to go —
The Path that’s founded on Ambrosia—
So I in silent study pondering
Shall to the silence of the seers attain,
As glides great Ganga s river to the main.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXLV: Vitasoka
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
‘Now let him shave me!’ — so the barber came.
From him I took the mirror and, therein
Reflected, on myself I gazed and thought:

‘Futile for lasting is this body shown.’
[Thus thinking on the source that blinds our sight
My spirit’s] darkness melted into light.
Stripped are the swathing vestments utterly!
Now is there no more coming back to be?

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXLVI: Punnamasa
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
All the five Hindrances that bar the way
Against the safe, sure peace I put aside.
The mirror of the holy Norm I grasped: —
The knowing and the seeing what we are —

So I reflected on this grouped frame
Within and eke without, and I beheld
How, whether it was mine or not of me,
The body empty [is and vanity].

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXLVII: Nandaka
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
E’en though he trip and fall, the mettled brute
Of noble breed will steadfast stand once more.
Incited yet again to effort new,
Foredone no longer, draws his load along.

So look on me as one who having learned
Of Him, the all-enlightened One, and gained
True insight, am become of noble breed,
And of the Very Buddha son indeed.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXLVIII: Bharata
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Come, Nandaka, now go we unto Him
Whose blessed teaching taught us all we know;
And in the presence of the Wake, the Chief,
Let’s roar the lion’s paean of our hearts.

That quest for which the holy Sage in [love
And great] compassion bade us both go forth —
That Good supreme both you and I have won,
And every bond that hindered us is gone.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CXLIX: Bharadvaja
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Tis thus th’ enlightened lift their triumph-song,
Like lions roaring in the hill-ravine,
Heroes who in the holy war have won,
And conquered evil, Mara and his host.

The servant of the blessed Master I,
A votary of the Norm and Brotherhood;
And glad and gratified my heart to see
My son purged of the poisons, sane, immune.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CL: Kanhadinna
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Waited have I on saintly men and heard
Full many times the saving truths [they taught].
Hearing I knew I should attain the road
That leads away from things that age and die.

And so in me all lust to live again
Thus being utterly cast out, since then
In me tis no more found, nor was’t, nor will it e’er
Come back in me, nor at this hour doth rise in me.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CLI: Migasira
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Since I went forth and entered on the Rule
Ordained by the Enlightened One Supreme,
Emancipated as I went, I rose
Transcending all these things of sense-desire.

While He, that Very Brahmin, looked on me,
O then my heart was set at liberty!
Yea, since all bonds are broke for evermore,
For me Emancipation’s fixed and sure!

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CLII: Sivaka
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Transient the little houses [of our life],
Built here, built there, again, ever again.
Hunting the house-builder [thus far I come];
Birth is but woe again, ever again.

Thou’rt found, house-maker thou, thou’rt seen at last!
Never again shalt fashion house [for me]!
Broken are all thy walls, shattered thy roofs.
Stayed is the further rise of consciousness;
Blown ’twill be even here to nothingness.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CLIII: Upavana
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
The Arahant, the Well-Come of all men,
The Holy Sage, he suffereth sore with wind.
If there be any water heated here,
O give it to me, brahmin, for the Sage.

Revered by them to whom we reverence owe,
Cherished by them who claim our pious care,
Honoured by them to whom honour is due,
For Him I do beseech it may be brought.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CLIV: Isidinna
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
I mark the pious laity who treasure on their lips the Norm;
How you may often hear them say: ‘Transient are
all this world’s desires!’
But in their hearts lies love of pelf, of precious stones and jewelled rings,
And that which fills their thought is care of sons and
daughters and of wives.

Nay, verily, they do not know the inward meaning of the Norm;
E’en though you often hear them say: ‘Transient are
all this world’s desires!’
To cut themselves from passions free, they lack the spiritual health,
And therefore cleaveth aye their heart to wife and
children, and to wealth.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CLV: Sambula-Kaccana
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
God’s rain pours down, ay, and god’s rain roars down,
And I alone in fearsome hollow dwell.
Yet dwelling so in fearsome rocky dell
To me no fear comes nigh, no creeping dread,
No quailing [of my soul].

For such the law
Within the blessed Norm, that dwelling so
To me no fear comes nigh, no creeping dread,
No quailing [of my soul] to me, alone.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CLVI: Khitaka
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Whose heart stands like a rock, and swayeth not,
Void of all lust for things that lust beget,
And all unshaken in a shifting world?
To heart thus trained, whence shall come aught of ill?

My heart stands like a rock, and swayeth not,
Void of all lust for things that lust beget,
And all unshaken in a shifting world.
My heart thus trained— whence shall come ill to me?

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CLVII: Sona-Potiriyaputta
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Nay, not for this that thou mayest slumber long,
Cometh the night in starry garlands wreathed.
For vigil by the wise this night is here.

If in the light my warrior-elephant
Advanced, ’twere better, fallen from his back,
Dead on the field [and trampled I should lie],
Than beaten live a captive to the foe.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CLVIII: Nisabha
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Put them away, those fivefold things of sense,
Objects that charm and captivate the mind.
Thou who through faith didst give up home and world,
Become end-maker of its grief and pain.

With thought of death I dally not, nor yet
Delight in living. I await the hour
With mind discerning and with heedfulness.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CLIX: Usabha
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
A cloak the hue of purple mango-buds
Draping about my shoulder, I bestrode
The back of elephant, and so to seek
Mine alms into the village street I rode.

Down from his back [in very shame] I slid —
[When lo! I woke and] anguish seized me then.
This arrogant self was then made meek and mild,
Purged were the poisons [that my mind defiled].

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CLX: Kappata-kura
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
‘These,’ saith he, ‘are the rags of Rags-and-Rice I
Too heavy is the gear I’m wearing now.’
Full measure of the Norm hath he in shower
Ambrosial; and yet no step he takes
To practise contemplative discipline.

O Kappata, thou shouldst not sway and nod,
Nor make me cuff the word into thine ear.
Never a whit thou, Kappata, hast learned,
Sleepily swaying ’midst the listeners here.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CLXI: Kumara-Kassapa
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
All hail the Buddhas, and all hail the Norms.
Hail the blest System by our Master wrought,
Wherein he that doth hear may [be enrolled
And] come to realize a Norm like ours.

Down countless ages have its members come,
Reborn now as this compound, now as that.
But this for them is now the very last,
The final confluence of the factors five,
In flux of rebirth and mortality.
Now come they never more again to be.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CLXII: Dhammapala
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
The brother who while young hath given himself
Wholly to carry out the Buddha’s plan,
Who keepeth vigil in a sleeping world,
Not vainly, not for naught he spends his days.

So let the wise man, so let him who aye
Remembereth that which Buddhas have enjoined,
Devote himself to faith and righteousness,
To know the blessedness They brought to us,
And the true vision of the holy Norm.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CLXIII: Brahmali
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
In whom the senses have been hushed to calm,
Like horses well tamed by the charioteer,
In whom no vain conceits are found, nor aught
Of poison-fumes survives, a man like this
May stir up envy e’en among the gods.

In me the senses have been hushed to calm,
Like horses well tamed by the charioteer,
In me no vain conceits are found, nor aught
Of poison-fumes survives; — one such as I
May stir up envy e’en among the gods.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CLXIV: Mogharajan
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Well, Mogharajan, thou skin-sufferer,
Thou blest of heart and constantly serene,
Cometh the time when winter nights are cold,
And thou a brother poor — how wilt thou fare?

Rich are the cornfields of the Magadhese,
And thriving, every one, I’ve heard it said.
My little straw-built canopy doth please
Better than others’ way of finding ease.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CLXV: Visakha the Pancali’s Son
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Let him not be puffed up, nor other folk
Belittle, nor despise nor yet molest
The victor who hath overcome the world.
Nor let him drag the praises of himself
Before the public; let him be sober, meek,
And moderate in speech and virtuous.

Is there a man who can the truth discern,
Tho’ it be very subtle and refined?
Who skilled to measure spiritual growth,
Is yet of lowly, and of gentle mind.
Who shapes his life by rule of Them that Wake:
For him, Nibbana is not hard to find.

poems.title: Psalms of the Brethren CLXVI: Culaka
poems.author: The Brethren of the Theragatha
poems.collection: Psalms of the Early Buddhists II: Psalms of the Brethren (1913)
poems.translator: trans. Mrs. C. A. F. Rhys Davids (1913)
poems.text:
Hark! how the peacocks make the welkin ring,
Fair-crested, fine their plumes and azure throat,
Graceful in shape and pleasant in their cry.
And see how this broad landscape watered well
Lies verdure-clad beneath the dappled sky!

Healthy thy frame and fit and vigorous
To make good progress in the Buddha’s rule.
Come then and grasp the rapt thought of the saint,
And touch the crystal bright, the subtly deep,
The elusive mystery — even the Way
